resources.string: A local-first foundation for safe phone-to-phone assistance.
The authenticated protocol foundation is being developed. Live phone-to-phone transport and backup restore are not available yet.

No rescue session, backup, restore, screen sharing, remote unlock, or file access is active. This build uses Android Keystore for a local identity and requests network and Wi-Fi multicast-state permissions only for user-started local service discovery. It does not request Bluetooth, camera, storage, or accessibility permissions.
These values come from Android system build properties. They are identifying strings, not a complete hardware-health assessment.
Rescue access must be explicitly enrolled, limited to a specific operation, authenticated, time-bounded, and revocable. A previously paired device does not receive unrestricted access.

A standalone Kotlin module defines mutual peer authentication, ephemeral ECDH key agreement, HKDF-SHA-256 key derivation, and AES-GCM records with sequence-based replay rejection. It is not yet wired to an Android transport or backup flow.
The app does not bypass Android authentication, extract protected keys, exploit debugging, install silently, capture screens silently, or claim remote unlocking.
